description: The update rule every Docker app extends, as github>jterrazz/studio-actions//renovate/apps. Two lanes.
Routine lane: base images only, weekly, and never a version younger than 3 days, the window in which a hijacked or broken release is usually caught and pulled.
A floating minor tag where the publisher offers one (node:24-alpine, oven/bun:1.4, ubuntu:26.04) takes its patches at build time, so it is left alone: never moved, never pinned by digest.
An exact version (eceasy/cli-proxy-api:v8.0.44) moves weekly: a patch merges itself once every check on its PR is green; a minor or a major stays a PR the owner reviews.

Security lane: a version that fixes a known vulnerability (GitHub's Dependabot alerts, and OSV for direct npm dependencies), in base images and npm packages alike, opens at once, skips the schedule and the 3-day wait, and merges itself on green checks: once a fix is public, its exploit is hours away.

packageRules.description: npm dependencies move only through the security lane: routine npm updates stay the repository's own business. The security lane's `enabled: true` re-enables a vulnerable one, as Renovate's security:only-security-updates preset does.
A tag that is not an exact x.y.z (a floating major or minor, a codename) is the publisher's to move.

Renovate merges the patch itself, and only on green checks: a private repository on this plan holds no branch protection, so GitHub's auto-merge has no required check to wait for. A repository whose PRs run no check never automerges.
